note: Two-layer discharge. evidence_mechanism proves the CODE FACT (cheap: replayable against a baseline commit with no running app, no seeded DB, no fault injection). inference_mechanism proves the HARM FOLLOWS (often expensive: needs a runtime). FP measurement lives at the evidence layer. The claim types are stack-independent; only the concrete checker binding varies, keyed under `stacks` (ts-prisma | php-laravel | py-sqlalchemy).

stacks.ts-prisma: a .catch()/try-catch whose handler discards the rejection reason; literal form is load-bearing (.catch(null) is a no-op, not a swallow)
stacks.php-laravel: try/catch returning a rewritten response without rethrow
stacks.py-sqlalchemy: except that passes or returns a sentinel, dropping the exception

stacks.php-laravel: no audit model write / no Event dispatch on the action
stacks.py-sqlalchemy: no audit-row insert in the unit of work

stacks.ts-prisma: resolver acts on a child id without a where-clause tying it to the authorised parent
stacks.php-laravel: no policy/gate binding the route parameter to the actor
stacks.py-sqlalchemy: query filters by resource id only, not by owner

stacks.ts-prisma: two writes not wrapped in prisma.$transaction(cb)
stacks.py-sqlalchemy: writes spanning a commit boundary / not in one session.begin()

stacks.ts-prisma: side effect dispatched after prisma.$transaction resolves
stacks.php-laravel: job/mail dispatched after DB::transaction() returns (not afterCommit-guarded)

stacks.ts-prisma: deleteMany/updateMany with a where-clause missing a discriminating column
stacks.php-laravel: Eloquent mass delete/update without the guarding scope
stacks.py-sqlalchemy: bulk delete()/update() query missing a filter clause

stacks.ts-prisma: a read used as a guard for a later write with no row lock / unique constraint between them

MUTABLE_CAPTURE_ACROSS_RETRY.note: candidate type — mechanism undetermined until the falsification test admits it
